summary: The team is executing a two-front push — SEO/AI-search visibility for Asia Star and the new Intelligent China program, plus the Knowledge website redesign — while clearing this week's operational blockers and laying groundwork for the 2026 Women in Leadership Forum and APEC.
summaryDetail: The top priority remains the global marketing strategy: Asia Star and Intelligent China are locked in as the lead programs for SEO/AI-search visibility, with US partner programs (Berkeley as the likely third) on hold pending the audit. That work now hinges on Joseph drafting the target areas/prompts and the team auditing Google Ads conversion tracking once the setup brief lands, alongside driving traffic to the Intelligent China page. On the Knowledge website redesign, the team has settled on the current two-menu structure with improved categorization and dispersed topic-based videos, but needs to close the loop: Joseph, Julie and the team lead must hold the 30-minute feedback session so Joker can implement changes, and Joseph still owes the inspirational HTML file. This week's urgent operational item is the Outlook lockout — clear stale saved passwords, re-authenticate on all devices, and confirm the backend account is unlocked with CKGSB. Looking ahead, attention is turning to the 2026 Women in Leadership Forum design (brand feedback due from Celine's team and Ira), the APEC concept note with Shengjia, LinkedIn paid-solutions exploration, and a stronger CKGSB Monthly banner via Flow while the school PPT copy slips two weeks pending the dean's comments.
